{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-tn","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"3159efa50ac85a606590142d0d100d5afbc32b8664c04222aee8e7b7de26dd8b","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-tn-class-d:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"8b0b6a068a0aa720d419171b5007a2610ed6c5012eeff522b57713cf9226eb71","source_liveness_sha256":"d27b9a94f03ec29d960b8eea38966606a7d3fdb703ad30b19ecd93f9bc70d0c7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"License class confusables and credential details","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: look-alike class and endorsement letters, exempt versus ineligible drivers, temporary credentials and add-on designations","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: look-alike class and endorsement letters, exempt versus ineligible drivers, temporary credentials and add-on designations
Confusable pairs among license classes and endorsement letters, then continuation facts on exemptions, refusals, temporary credentials and optional designations; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A01
The letter H means two different things on the license chart: Class H is the hardship license for young drivers, while the H endorsement covers hazardous materials. [A01]
Why it matters: group license classes; confusable Class H versus H endorsement.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A01
The letter P also does double duty: Class P is an instructional permit, while the P endorsement covers vehicles designed to seat 16 or more people including the driver. [A01]
Why it matters: group license classes; confusable Class P versus P endorsement.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A01
The N endorsement covers tanks holding 1,000 gallons or more, and the X endorsement combines tanks with hazardous materials. [A01]
Why it matters: group endorsements; difficulty medium; commercial scope note.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A01
The T endorsement covers double and triple trailers, and the S endorsement covers school buses. [A01]
Why it matters: group endorsements; difficulty low; commercial scope note.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A02
The manual describes the For-Hire endorsement as a bridge between the regular license for private travel and the commercial license needed for tractor-trailers, large trucks and buses. [A02]
Why it matters: group endorsements; confusable For-Hire versus CDL.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A03
Class M can be issued as a license on its own or alongside another primary class on the same card. [A03]
Why it matters: group license classes; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A03
Hardship licenses are rare: fewer than one percent of the licenses issued to minors are Class H. [A03]
Why it matters: group hardship; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A04
Members of the armed forces, National Guard included, need no Tennessee license while driving a vehicle owned or leased by the military. [A04]
Why it matters: group exemptions; confusable exempt versus ineligible.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A04
Operators of road machinery, farm tractors or other farm equipment moved temporarily along a highway need no Tennessee license. [A04]
Why it matters: group exemptions; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A04
Visitors carrying a valid license from their home state or country, equivalent to the matching Tennessee class, may drive without a Tennessee license. [A04]
Why it matters: group exemptions; confusable visitor versus new resident.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A04
Students in a Department-approved driver training course at a school or licensed driving school may drive unlicensed only while a certified instructor accompanies them. [A04]
Why it matters: group exemptions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A04
A license is refused to anyone suspended or revoked in any state, anyone who has not shown required proof of insurance or financial responsibility, and anyone the Commissioner finds unable to drive safely because of a mental or physical disability. [A04]
Why it matters: group ineligibility; confusable exempt versus ineligible.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A04
An applicant who has never had a Social Security number signs an affidavit under penalty of perjury and supplies a certified US birth certificate or valid US passport, or USCIS proof of permanent residence. [A04]
Why it matters: group identification; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A04
Families may get identification-only licenses for children, even infants, as long as each child meets the documentation requirements. [A04]
Why it matters: group identification; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A05
Temporary legal presence is usually proven with an I-551, I-688 or I-766 card or a valid foreign passport with visa and I-94, and F1 or F2 holders add a SEVIS I-20 while J1 or J2 holders add a DS-2019. [A05]
Why it matters: group temporary credentials; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A05
A TDL can be issued as a learner permit (XPD, XMPD) or a combination type (XDM), proves the holder passed Tennessee's Class D or M requirements, and also works as identification. [A05]
Why it matters: group temporary credentials; confusable TDL versus TID.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A05
Circling YES for donation on a license or ID application places you on the Donate Life Tennessee registry as legal consent, and removing the red heart later requires a duplicate license at a Driver Service Center. [A05]
Why it matters: group designations; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A06
An honorably discharged veteran can have Veteran printed on the license by certifying it on the application and showing a certified DD-214, a NAVPERS-660 discharge certificate or a DD Form 2 (Retired) card. [A06]
Why it matters: group designations; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-R19 | anchor: A06
An International Driving Permit is only a translation of a home license, must travel with that license, and is never valid by itself or for driving inside the United States. [A06]
Why it matters: group international; misconception IDP as a license.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-R20 | anchor: A06
Tennessee Driver Service Centers do not issue International Driving Permits; residents ask a local AAA office, and foreign visitors must obtain one in their home country before arriving. [A06]
Why it matters: group international; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-R21 | anchor: A06
Registered sexual or violent sexual offenders must tell the examiner when applying or renewing, complete a Sex Offender Declaration and Supplemental Application, and carry their license or ID at all times. [A06]
Why it matters: group special applicants; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-R22 | anchor: A06
The Driver Service Center only forwards a voter application to the County Election Commission, because only the Election Registrar can issue a voter registration card. [A06]
Why it matters: group designations; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0020]
